A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fine-tuning unlearning research, retaining the linear-regression framework, Theorems 1–3, and associated simulations despite changes to the title and practical method. Both versions are readable and complete for comparison, including figures, tables, and Appendices A–B.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic simulations and ResNet-18 unlearning experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN, including sensitivity results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original masking experiments for class-wise and random forgetting on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, alongside retained synthetic simulations.

M1.justification: V1's practical KL-based discriminative regularization is replaced by Retention-Based Masking in v2 Section 5. The new procedure freezes weights salient on the remaining data and updates their complement using random-label forgetting and retaining cross-entropy losses. The idealized feature-removal procedure in Section 4 already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates class-wise forgetting on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN. V2 retains the CIFAR class-wise tasks, adds random forgetting on both CIFAR datasets, and removes SVHN. The synthetic distinct/overlapping-feature scenarios and the six t-SNE class examples are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding CIFAR comparisons replace CE-FT and ICE-FT with SalUn, while retaining Retrain and naive FT; KL-FT also disappears from the reported comparisons. V1 explicitly disables SalUn's masking component when constructing its CE-FT comparison, whereas v2 evaluates masked SalUn, so this is a substantive comparator change rather than renaming.

E3.justification: V2 adds average disparity to the existing evaluation metrics. Its new masked-method comparisons specify 50% sparsity and ten unlearning epochs, reduced to five for CIFAR-100 random forgetting. The ResNet-18 backbone and individual accuracy metrics remain; newly disclosed training settings do not establish changes to previously unspecified v1 settings.

E4.justification: V2 removes the regularization-strength sensitivity study, including the KL-FT sweep and CE-FT versus ICE-FT analysis in v1 Figure 4 and Appendix Table 4. No corresponding masking sensitivity study replaces it. The fine-tuning sample-size simulations, overlapping-feature retention/discarding comparison, and t-SNE case study remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports means and standard deviations over five independent trials; v2 explicitly describes five seeds. This clarifies the repetitions' seed basis, while retaining the repetition count and uncertainty-reporting practice. It does not establish additional runs or introduce confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The real-world result set is substantially replaced. For example, Table 2 reports class-wise FT unlearning accuracy of 20.89% versus 8.36% on CIFAR-10 and 34.44% versus 11.55% on CIFAR-100 in v1 versus v2. V2 adds RBM/SalUn and random-forgetting results while removing the regularization, SVHN, and sensitivity entries. Identical training conditions across versions are not established, so these are reported-result changes rather than demonstrated same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3 and the Appendix B derivations retain their substantive assumptions, arguments, and conclusions. V2 incorporates existing remarks into assumptions, explicitly writes the existing MSE losses, and corrects notation and dimensional typos. It adds no separate theoretical analysis of the gradient-derived RBM procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion replace discriminative regularization as the practical contribution with RBM and claims of superior retention and lower average disparity relative to forgetting-based masking. V2 also attributes theoretical benefits directly to RBM. The central explanation of naive fine-tuning's failure and the claimed first linear-regression analysis remain.

C2.justification: The central interpretation that preserving overlapping features protects retention remains. V2 applies it specifically to retention-derived saliency masks and interprets lower average disparity as improved balance. It removes v1's explicit warning that the structured assumptions may fail in practice and its proposed extensions of discriminative regularization to other unlearning methods.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A.2 substantially expands implementation documentation: 182 pretraining epochs, initial learning rate 0.1 with cosine decay, SGD, method-specific unlearning learning rates, epoch budgets, and 50% sparsity. Conversely, v1's batch-size-256 disclosure is removed. These are documentation changes and settings for the new comparisons, not proof that retained experiments changed every listed setting.

R1.justification: The practical research positioning changes substantially: v1 distinguishes its method through loss choice and regularization emphasis, whereas v2 identifies shared-feature preservation as a gap in SalUn and positions retention-based saliency as the remedy. SalUn was already cited in v1. The general related-work survey remains largely unchanged, and the SVHN reference is removed.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and author list and extensively rewrites the abstract, contribution bullets, practical-method discussion, experimental interpretation, and conclusion. The formerly separate method and experiment sections become Section 5 with experiments in Section 5.2. Appendix A.2 is rewritten, and masking terminology replaces regularization terminology throughout the retained theoretical discussion.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Table 2 into four CIFAR task blocks and adds disparity columns, removes v1's radar and sensitivity figures and Appendix Tables 3–4, and restyles or repositions retained simulation plots. The t-SNE display is retained as Figure 3 rather than Figure 5. These changes substantially revise the experimental presentation.

improvement.justification: The full SalUn comparison, random-forgetting evaluations, and expanded training documentation strengthen practical support. However, v2 removes SVHN and sensitivity evidence, makes stronger RBM-specific theoretical claims while retaining the idealized proofs, and introduces conflicting RA/MIA assignments between Tables 1 and 2, which agreed in v1. These substantive gains and weaknesses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
